base_amount_policy.dynamic_first_allocation_scale: The first same-day allocation per ticker selects the base BEFORE the ladder multiplier: below the prior regular-session close AND the prior regular-session low -> $2.00 (base_amount_usd); below the prior close only (not below the prior low) -> $1.00 (base_amount_below_close_usd); not below the prior close -> no buy. A missing prior low is treated as not-below-low ($1.00).
base_amount_policy.candidate_dollar_formula: candidate_dollar_amount = selected_base_amount_usd * multiplier, where selected_base_amount_usd is $1.00 or $2.00 per the dynamic_first_allocation_scale.
base_amount_policy.no_fallback: Never infer, discover, or fall back to $50.00 or any broker/account default base amount. The base is exactly $1.00 or $2.00 per the dynamic scale.

risk_guard.description: Dynamic risk guard. A rolling 30-day cash-burn rate is tracked for visibility. When capital deployed in any trailing 7-day window exceeds kill_switch_7d_deploy_fraction (40%) of monthly_cash_allocation_usd, the graded ladder is capped at 1x: the strategy keeps buying dips at the base amount but stops scaling up until the 7-day window rolls back under the threshold. Deployment is counted only from scheduled-live afternoon evidence (run_origin='scheduled', manual_run=false, timestamp at/after 2:30 PM ET); manual and other streams are excluded. See docs/risk_management.md and dca_risk.py.

budget_tiers_runtime_status: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- NOT READ AT RUNTIME. Editing the numbers in budget_tiers below changes NOTHING about live behavior. The authoritative tier ladder is hardcoded in near_close_dca.py as BUDGET_TIERS (the daily/weekly cap pairs), TIER_SPEND_THRESHOLDS_USD (129.0, 213.0, 272.0) and TIER_HIGH_MULTIPLIER_SIGNAL_THRESHOLDS (5, 10, 17); dca_config.load_budgets() deliberately does not map this block onto StrategyConfig ('The budget_tiers block in budgets.json is documentation of that ladder; it is not a StrategyConfig field and is intentionally not applied'). The two are kept in sync BY HAND, pinned by test_config_invariants.py. To actually change a cap or threshold you must edit near_close_dca.py AND mirror it here, or the pinning test fails. Flagged 2026-08-03 because nothing in this file previously said so, and a maintainer could reasonably assume editing these values took effect.

budget_tiers.name: normal
budget_tiers.escalate_above_planned_spend_usd_note: NON-GATING. Documentation/monitoring reference only -- tier selection does not key on planned spend. See selection_rule.

budget_tiers.name: elevated
budget_tiers.escalate_above_planned_spend_usd_note: NON-GATING. Documentation/monitoring reference only -- tier selection does not key on planned spend. See selection_rule.

budget_tiers.name: high_volatility
budget_tiers.escalate_above_planned_spend_usd_note: NON-GATING. Documentation/monitoring reference only -- tier selection does not key on planned spend. See selection_rule.

budget_tiers.name: stress
budget_tiers.note: Effective weekly budget: min($1,800, $900 + available_prior_unused_rollover_reserve). With no rollover: $900 available. With full $900 rollover: $1,800 available. Rollover is prior-week unused budget that supplements this tier's base allocation.
budget_tiers.rollover_reserve_reconciliation: Stress tier effective weekly cap = min(nominal_tier_cap=$1,800, normal_tier_base=$900 + available_rollover_reserve). The tier always has a budget to spend; absence of rollover means a $900 effective budget (same as the Normal tier), not an abort condition. Examples: (1) $0 prior rollover → $900 effective; (2) $500 prior rollover → $1,400 effective; (3) $900+ prior rollover → $1,800 effective (capped). This reconciliation formula is enforced in near_close_dca.StrategyState.effective_weekly_cap() and removes the ambiguity that was triggering Gate 8 aborts.

selection_rule: Pick the tier keyed SOLELY on the count of 3x-or-greater signals in the Gate 7 candidate list (fixed before sizing runs): Normal <=5, Elevated 6-10, High-volatility 11-17, Stress >17. A 3x-or-greater signal is a buy candidate whose ladder multiplier is >= 3.0. Tier selection must NEVER key on planned spend, which is an output of the sizing decision, not an input fixed before it -- each tier's escalate_above_planned_spend_usd is retained only as a non-gating documentation/monitoring reference (see the per-tier escalate_above_planned_spend_usd_note fields).
allocation_priority: Prioritize allocations by higher multiplier first, then larger percent drop, then ticker (alphabetical) for a deterministic tie-break. Flag any capped tickers.

robinhood.note: Only execution broker/account for live and manual runs.

alpaca.note: Read-only validation and account context only; never execution unless explicitly changed later.

finance.note: Read-only market-data/validation context only; never execution.

market_data_source_policy.summary: The Finance connector is the PRIMARY market-data source. Alpaca and Robinhood provide validation / context. There is no fallback source: an unavailable or incomplete primary aborts the run (the Finance-primary 3:30 slot reconciles on Robinhood alone). Robinhood remains the only execution broker.
market_data_source_policy.gfuz_exception: GFUZ may use Robinhood as its PRIMARY source when the Finance connector cannot resolve it (see config/tickers.json:special_handling.GFUZ).

safety_policy: No sells, options, crypto, margin changes, account modifications, or order cancellations unless explicitly requested later. Buys only, regular market hours only, one strategy order per ticker per stream per day.

execution_authorization_policy.description: As approved Fri Jul 10 2026 11:20 AM ET, scheduled live DCA tasks are pre-authorized to auto-place qualifying buys within all caps and circuit breakers WITHOUT per-order human confirmation.

scheduled_tasks.placement_precondition: May call place_equity_order directly ONLY after every internal validation, signal, budget, spread, confidence/trend, and top-up check passes.
scheduled_tasks.note: Scheduled live tasks must NOT request per-order confirmation and must NOT call Robinhood review_equity_order (which forces a preview + confirmation).

manual_tasks.note: Manual / ad hoc runs still use the review + confirmation path before any placement.

circuit_breakers.max_consecutive_placement_failures_note: THE knob for how many placements may fail BACK TO BACK before a live batch stops attempting the remainder. Added 2026-08-24 to replace halt-on-first-rejection, which produced 'GS, EVR: never submitted -- batch halted after RVII rejection' and 'batch stopped mid-way at Gate 9, 34 of 37 planned buys placed, 3 tickers not bought'. One ticker's rejection is that ticker's problem (an untradable symbol, a stale quote, a broker-side refusal) and must never cost the tickers behind it their buy; a RUN of consecutive failures is a different signal -- the broker leg itself is unhealthy (outage, expired session, account block, exhausted buying power) -- and continuing would only submit more doomed orders. Enforced in dca_runner.execute_plan (MAX_CONSECUTIVE_PLACEMENT_FAILURES) and mirrored in the Gate 7 instruction of every executor prompt under claude/dca-executor-prompts/. Must be an integer >= 1; 1 restores the old halt-on-first-rejection behavior. Independent of the streak: the window closing mid-batch and a failed audit write still stop the batch immediately, and a failed order is still never retried within the same run.
circuit_breakers.whole_share_max_per_order_note: The per-order ceiling used ONLY by the whole-share accumulation path (near_close_dca._whole_share_risk_gates, StrategyConfig.whole_share_max_per_order_usd), added 2026-08-24. A whole-share ticker cannot be bought in any unit smaller than ONE SHARE, so max_per_order_usd's $10 -- sized for fractional dollar orders, where any amount is expressible -- reads as 'never buy this ticker at all' for any symbol trading above it. That blocked RVII (~$23/share) outright the moment it moved into the whole_share category, and BYDDY (~$10/share) clears the $10 cap by only a cent or two. DELIBERATELY NARROW: this authorizes exactly ONE share that the ordinary ceiling cannot fit, and never enlarges a multi-share fire -- how many shares may go into one order is still max_per_order_usd's decision, so BYDDY keeps buying 1 share at ~$10 rather than 5 at $50. It also never applies while the deployment kill switch is capping the executable fire (ceiling_override_usd), which must keep blocking. $50 clears RVII with room for roughly a 2x move; raising it raises the maximum a single whole-share order can spend, so change it deliberately. Must be a finite positive number and must never be BELOW max_per_order_usd (dca_config rejects that, since it would silently tighten the ordinary ceiling on this path instead of being the allowance it is). Daily/weekly budget caps, the spread gate, and the order-count cap all still apply on top.
circuit_breakers.max_per_order_note: 8x * $2 base = $16 is the absolute per-order ceiling for every FRACTIONAL (notional dollar) order, on all live streams. The reduced $1 below-close-only base tops out at 8x * $1 = $8, so the $16 ceiling is unchanged. ONE carve-out, added 2026-08-24: a ticker in tickers.json's whole_share list has no purchasable unit smaller than one share, so its single-share fire is measured against whole_share_max_per_order_usd instead -- see whole_share_max_per_order_note for the exact, deliberately narrow scope. Nothing else may exceed $16.
skip_conditions: skip if the bid/ask spread is too wide
skip if the intraday trend cannot be validated down (flag manual_review_candidate instead of buying)
skip a top-up if the current price is not strictly below the prior same-day buy reference price

skip if it would exceed the max per-order $10 ceiling (whole_share tickers: skip if it would exceed whole_share_max_per_order_usd instead -- one share only, and never while the deployment kill switch is capping the fire)
skip if it would exceed the selected daily or weekly cap
skip if it would exceed available buying power
skip any ticker not on the active whitelist
skip if a strategy order for that ticker was already placed in this stream today
circuit_breakers.max_orders_per_day_note:
THE knob for how many orders a day the roster may place, shared across all seven slots AND manual buying. Change this one number to raise or lower it; nothing else needs editing. Counted as buy ATTEMPTS for the trading day in America/New_York (BrokerOrder.is_buy_attempt), so a cancelled or rejected buy still consumes one -- the conservative direction. Enforced on the afternoon live path in near_close_dca.within_caps() (StrategyConfig.max_orders_per_day, overlaid from this value by dca_config.load_strategy_config); also enforced in dca_runner.plan_orders() as SKIPPED_DAILY_ORDER_COUNT_CAP for the separate assess()/plan_orders() path. As of 2026-08-03 (Codex review: 'Enforce the shared daily order-count cap in new executors'), MorningDCAExecutor._place_broker_orders (morning_dca.py, MorningConfig.max_orders_per_day, overlaid from this same value by load_morning_config/load_stream_config) also enforces it for the morning/midday/market-open/intraday streams -- the executors an external scheduler/agent invokes directly, not through run_dca.run_slot()/run_pipeline(). Its cross-stream seed is an approximation (one attempt per distinct ticker with a positive same-day prior allocation, not a true per-attempt count -- see MorningDCAExecutor._compute_top_up's cap_seed_roots block), so it can undercount a ticker topped up more than once in a day. Both stop the batch at the boundary rather than back-filling smaller orders.

2026-09-11 CHANGED from 8 to 120 (Geoff's direction, after a monitoring pass found this had effectively never bound live trading). 8 sat far below the active roster's own size (config/tickers.json's 'active' list has 59 tickers), so on any day the graded ladder legitimately touched a double-digit slice of the roster across the seven slots -- ordinary, correctly-functioning operation, not a malfunction -- the count already exceeded 8; a 2026-09-10 single-slot run alone placed 45 orders. Treating 8 as a real ceiling was therefore never viable without a fundamentally different strategy (few, large positions instead of many small dip-buys), which is NOT what the $180 daily_cap_usd / $900 weekly_cap_usd tiers above are sized for. 120 is a HEURISTIC breaker, roughly 2x the 59-ticker active roster -- NOT a precise structural derivation: same_day_top_up_policy (config/scheduled_tasks.json) permits a ticker to be topped up repeatedly across different slots at successively deeper prices, and real trading days have done exactly that (2026-07-30/07-31 incident notes in config/scheduled_tasks.json record TRIN and SPCX each bought 3x in one day), so 'one initial buy plus one top-up per ticker' is not actually the ceiling this design enforces -- the true structural max per ticker is bounded only by the seven scheduled slots (plus manual buying), i.e. up to 7-8 attempts on one ticker alone in a pathological but policy-compliant day. 120 is chosen to sit comfortably above every real day cited above (15, 45) with wide margin while remaining well short of a number that would only trip on genuine runaway/duplicate-batch behavior; it is not derived from a maximum-repeat invariant and should be revisited if real order-history analysis suggests a different number. This is now a RARE-EVENT / RUNAWAY-BATCH circuit breaker -- it should almost never bind in normal operation -- not a strategic per-day trade-count budget; the daily_cap_usd/weekly_cap_usd tiers remain the actual strategy-defining spend controls. Separately, and NOT fully fixed by this change: near_close_dca.within_caps()'s own seeding (_seed_prior_allocations) counts only the attempts THIS engine can see in its own local run_state*.json artifact tree, with no visibility into orders the standing Perplexity backup executor places directly against the same account (see claude/PERPLEXITY-CLAUDE-COORDINATION.md) -- that path's cap is per-engine, not per-account, until dca_runner.count_compatible_executor_attempts (added 2026-09-11, not yet wired in) is plugged into its seeding. The other six live-mirror prompts' Gate 6 (and the 3:30 PM prompt's own Gate 6, extended 2026-09-11 to also enforce this cap) compute their count directly from a freshly fetched, fully paginated get_equity_orders history and count every order 'regardless of placed_agent' -- those ARE already account-wide, provided that fetch is actually complete and fresh each time; MorningDCAExecutor's own Python ledger (morning_dca.py), by contrast, is local-artifact-seeded like near_close_dca's and not currently invoked by any live prompt (see docs/live_wiring.md).

order_rules.requires_review_before_submit: Manual runs: review_equity_order must pass first. Scheduled live runs are pre-authorized (see execution_authorization_policy) and call place_equity_order directly after all internal checks pass, without review_equity_order.
order_rules.one_order_per_ticker_per_day_note: Permanent policy, confirmed by Geoff 2026-08-02: the same ticker MAY be bought more than once in a day. same_day_top_up_policy (config/scheduled_tasks.json), enforced by scripts/same_day_top_up_gate.py, governs repeats: a later slot may buy the same ticker again, but only RESIZED to the incremental delta and only at a strictly lower price than the prior same-day reference. What stays blocked is a second buy within the SAME slot/session -- that is enforced separately by one_order_per_ticker_per_stream below, each stream's own sole-executor interlock (Gate 4), and the one-ticker-per-batch rule, not by this flag. dca_runner.assess() reads this flag directly from this file (no override) and no longer excludes a same-day-bought ticker outright; near_close_dca.StrategyConfig defaults to the same False for every caller. Do not set this back to true -- that would reintroduce the old first-slot-wins behavior this decision permanently retired.

hard_limits: Never exceed the max per-order $10 ceiling, the selected daily cap, the selected weekly cap, or available buying power. The single exception to the $10 figure is a whole_share ticker's one-share fire, which is bounded by whole_share_max_per_order_usd; every other cap here still applies to it unchanged. Caps are absolute ceilings; when a rule and an order conflict, the order is skipped.
